steps.say: This iPhone is mapping a room from a LiDAR on an Ethernet cable.
No laptop. The phone runs the whole thing.

scenes.headline: How an iPhone maps a room with a LiDAR
scenes.sub: Mobile SLAM: FAST-LIO's filter and NDT, in C++ on the phone
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Plumbob. Mobile SLAM's core is eleven hundred and eighty lines of C plus plus. Here is what they do.

scenes.title: From the jack to the filter

steps.say: The sensor stamps points and IMU with its own clock. The phone's sensors never enter the estimate.
A USB-C Ethernet adapter takes the address the sensor sends to.
Plain UDP sockets catch the packets. No Livox SDK.
If the filter falls behind, point packets are dropped, never IMU.
One worker thread feeds the filter.

steps.term: Deskew: undo the motion during a sweep
steps.say: The IMU predicts the motion during the sweep, and every point is moved to where it was really measured.
Each point fits a plane through five map neighbours. Its residual is the distance to that plane.
A gate drops points too far off, looser for distant ones.

steps.term: IESKF: an iterated error-state Kalman filter
steps.say: One cheap Kalman step. Re-associate and step again, at most four times.
Only then does the uncertainty shrink.

steps.caption: the Android app, keeping still
steps.say: Mapping starts with a second of standing still, to find the gyro bias and which way is down.

steps.caption: 146,581 points at 0:10
steps.say: Then you walk. Every tenth of a second, a sweep is deskewed, matched and added to the map.

left.title: FAST-LIO2
items: an ikd-Tree with exact nearest neighbours
a cube that slides with you
left.say: FAST-LIO2 keeps a tree of nearby points and deletes what falls behind you.

right.title: Mobile SLAM
items: 0.2 m hash voxels, one point each
right.say: Mobile SLAM keeps one point per voxel in a hash table. Fast, tiny, and it only grows.

scenes.title: Finding yourself in a saved map

params.search: no heading: 12 headings, five starts, 60 tries

steps.say: To localise, the saved map is cut into one metre cells, and each becomes a Gaussian.
A scan arrives slightly off. Climbing the score pulls it into the cells, and the pose goes into the filter.
With no heading, it tries twelve headings at five starting points.
It refines the best and accepts it when enough points match.

scenes.title: Where it stops short of survey grade
scenes.say: For scan to BIM, the gaps are specific.

items.say: No loop closure, so drift leaves walls drawn twice.
One raw return per cell, noise and all.
And a blind radius that hides most of a stair core.

scenes.text: Use the phone to record raw packets and check coverage. Do the mapping somewhere else.
scenes.say: Use the phone to record raw packets and check coverage on site. Map somewhere else.

recap: NDT relocalisation fused as a pose
A logger, not a survey instrument
